newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Oct bankruptcy debt soars to one-year high.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Oct bankruptcy debt soars to one-year high.

text.p: Total debt held by bankrupt firms in Japan in October nearly doubled from a year ago to 1.36 trillion yen, the highest level in a year, a private research and rating company said on Friday.

A large number of small and medium-sized firms continued to fold amid prolonged sluggishness in the economy combined with changes in the industrial structure, Tokyo Commerce and Industry Research Co said in a regular report on bankruptcies.
The October bankruptcy debt was the highest since September 1995, when the debt totalled 1.83 trillion yen.

Nevertheless, the biggest reason for the October surge was the failure of non-bank Nichiei Finance Co Ltd with total debts of more than one trillion yen, the largest insolvency case in Japan in the post-war period, it said.

The company, which is in the business of property-related financing and is classed in Japan as a non-bank financial institution, said it had applied to a Yokohama court for creditor protection under Japan's bankruptcy laws and would try to save what it could of its business with the court's help.
The firm said its borrowings totalled 170.89 billion yen at the end of September 1996 and that the debts it guaranteed totalled 820.65 billion yen on that same date.
Nichiei Finance, a unit of lumber firm Nichiei Co Ltd, has been hit hard by plummeting property prices since the bursting of Japan's 1980s "bubble economy" of inflated land and asset prices.

Japan has been swept by a wave of business failures since the bursting of the bubble. The economy is recovering from the post-bubble slump with the help of low interest rates and government stimulus measures, but the improvement is gradual.
But there were several good signs.
The number of companies filing for bankruptcy in Japan in October fell 0.7 percent from a year earlier to 1,391 cases, the report said.
The number of large-scale insolvencies involving total debts of more than one billion yen in October declined to 48, the lowest level in a year.

There were 832 business failures caused by weak economic conditions, accounting for 59 percent of the total. Of such cases, 655 bankruptcies were due to sluggish sales, 152 were due to accumulated losses and 25 were caused by trouble collecting money owed, the report said.
Bankruptcies in the construction sector went back up in October after falling for three consecutive months year-on-year. The figure rose 6.5 percent from a year ago to 390 cases.
The number of failures in the retail sector also jumped 30.1 percent from a year earlier to 207 cases.

Meanwhile, bankruptices in the manufacturing sector fell 9.3 percent to 281 cases in October. The wholesale and real estate sectors also saw the number of failures decline by 4.7 percent and 19.0 percent, respectively.
